executive_summary.headline: World risks are driving AMBER status: Strait of Hormuz transits down 97% year-on-year, Rhine waterways critically low, and energy prices elevated, whilst Infineon fell 5.5% today with no confirmed cause.
executive_summary.next_step: Verify whether Infineon's 5.5% drop correlates with the Strait of Hormuz transit collapse or other world-pillar shocks; check procurement routes and logistics costs for exposure to Rhine bottlenecks and energy surcharges in the next 48 hours.
executive_summary.context: Transits through the Strait of Hormuz have collapsed 97% compared to a year ago. The Rhine is critically constrained at both Kaub (1 cm, well below 40 cm threshold) and Maxau (281 cm, below 335 cm), creating shipping delays. Brent crude is 40% above its one-year median and EU natural gas 56% above July 2025; aluminium is 21% higher. Infineon, a high-exposure supplier, dropped unexpectedly without corroborating news, coinciding with these world-pillar constraints.
